summary: Iteration 22 — Ganti Password admin feature. Backend 6/6 pytest PASS: no-token→401, wrong current→400 'Password lama salah', new<6→400 'minimal 6', same-as-old→400 'berbeda', success→200 {ok:true} with old-pw login 401 and new-pw login 200, backend restart does NOT revert (seed_admin only inserts if missing — verified via sudo supervisorctl restart backend then re-login with newAdmin456), kasir (TEST_Iter22) can change own password & relogin (cleaned up). Frontend desktop E2E PASS: change-password-button opens change-pw-dialog, change-pw-error shows 'Password baru minimal 6 karakter' for <6 chars, 'Konfirmasi password tidak sama' for mismatch, server 'Password lama salah' for wrong current; change-pw-toggle flips input type password↔text; success closes dialog, fields cleared on reopen; after logout old pw login redirects back to /login and new pw logs in. Mobile (390x844) verified: mobile-menu-button opens sidebar with 'Ganti Password' visible at bottom (screenshot captured) and change-pw-dialog opens (verified earlier). Admin password restored to admin123 at end (both verified via /api/auth/login 200 for admin123 and 401 for newAdmin456).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py change_password validates current_password BEFORE length/same-as-old checks. If current is wrong you can never surface the length/same errors. Current order is actually safe (fail-fast on auth) and matches tests, but UI client-validates length/mismatch first so the server-side 'minimal 6' / 'berbeda' branches are mostly dead paths unless a non-UI client is used. Acceptable.
ChangePasswordDialog uses a single 'show' toggle for all 3 fields — fine for an admin-only screen but could leak the current password shoulder-surf. Low priority.

No rate limiting / brute-force protection on /auth/change-password — a stolen session token could brute-force the current_password. Consider throttling repeated wrong-current attempts (iter21 note still applies for /auth/login).

Login form (/login) inputs lack data-testid attributes (login-email/password/submit used but only present on Login page? Mobile verify used input[type=email] fallback). Not a bug for this iteration but worth adding for consistent E2E coverage.
server.py still ~1889 lines – carried-over suggestion to split into routers.
